sources.agency: Kentucky State Board of Elections, with the Division of Geographic Information and each county board of elections
sources.title: SBE Voting Precinct Boundaries (VTD_Boundaries)
sources.about: To support accurate and transparent election administration by providing a standardized spatial layer of voting precincts for use in other state and local GIS applications.
sources.use: This geospatial data set depicting Kentucky Voting Districts (VTD) is compiled by the Kentucky State Board of Elections from precinct boundary files submitted by the respective County Board of Elections of each of Kentucky's 120 counties. The State Board of Elections performs a compiling and procedural review function only, as authorized under KRS 117.055 to 117.0557, and does not originate, draw, or independently determine any precinct boundary or voter precinct assignment. Precinct boundaries are established, maintained, and controlled exclusively by each County Board of Elections, chaired by the County Clerk under KRS 117.035(3)(a), and remain subject to change as permitted by KRS 117.055 through 117.0557, including through a subsequently filed and approved Precinct Establishment Order.This precinct dataset is current through the November 3, 2026 General Election. Because precinct boundaries may be amended on each county's own timeline, this compiled precinct dataset may not reflect the most current precinct configuration at the moment of use, and does not reflect any Precinct Establishment Order filed or approved after the November 3, 2026 General Election. It is provided for general reference only and does not constitute the official legal record of precinct boundaries. For the authoritative and current boundary of a specific precinct, or for questions regarding voter precinct assignment, users should contact the County Clerk of the county in question. In the event of any conflict between this compiled precinct dataset and a county's own Precinct Establishment Order or precinct boundary records, the county's records control.

notes.lines: Every line is the State Board of Elections' precinct layer's, generalised by at most 1.5 metres and set on a grid of 0.00001 degree (about a metre). A point within a few metres of a line can fall on either side of it.
notes.precincts: The precinct layer is the State Board of Elections' compilation of the county boards' own precinct files; the publisher says it is current through the November 3, 2026 general election, that the county's own precinct records control where they differ, and that the county clerk is the authority on which precinct an address is in.
notes.districts: A precinct's congressional, Senate and House district and its Supreme Court district are the State Board of Elections' own word for it (its monthly registration report by precinct). A precinct may not cross any of those lines, or a justice of the peace or commissioner district's (KRS 117.055), so each is exact for the whole precinct.
notes.magisterial: A precinct code's letter is its magisterial district, as the State Board's report groups them. Which district a letter is was read from the State Board's 2026 primary and 2022 general recap sheets, whose precinct pages name the magistrate's and constable's contests on that precinct's ballot: usually A is the first district and B the second, but not in every county. A letter no sheet shows takes the alphabet's number only where every letter the sheets show follows it (supervisor_plans gives, county by county, each letter's district and how it was read; a letter not known has no com). Lexington-Fayette's own precinct table agrees with every Fayette precinct. Magistrates (justices of the peace) and constables are elected by the voters of their district. In a county whose fiscal court is three commissioners, the commissioner districts are the same lines (KRS 67.060), but each commissioner is elected by the whole county; supervisor_plans says which counties those are. Jefferson County's letters follow its House districts and give no magisterial district.
notes.places: Cities are the Census Bureau's 2025 places. A precinct lying wholly in one city names it (mcd); one that reaches into cities lists them (mcd_all, with each one's share of the precinct's area), and a precinct partly outside every city names no place of its own: the mcd layer answers for a point, cities first. In Jefferson County a voter in a city is a voter of the government too: every precinct there names the Louisville/Jefferson County metro government, which is all of the county, and the home rule cities it reaches.
notes.wards: Council districts are drawn for Louisville Metro (LOJIC's precinct table) and Lexington-Fayette (the Urban County Government's). Other cities' wards are not drawn.
notes.judicial: Judicial districts and circuits are whole counties (KRS 24A.030, 23A.020). The judicial layer draws the districts; a precinct also names its circuit, and its Supreme Court district, which is also its Court of Appeals district (KRS 22A.020).
notes.school: School district lines are the Census Bureau's 2025. Which districts a precinct lies in is analysis, not an official list: a district counts when its piece of the precinct is at least 60 metres thick somewhere; school_pct is each district's share of the precinct's area (land and water, not voters). An independent district's voters elect its board and not the county district's (KRS 160.210).
notes.soil: Every soil and water conservation supervisor contest on the list is filed under its county; the swcd layer draws the county.
notes.authority: For which precinct an address votes in, and where, the county clerk and the State Board of Elections' GoVoteKY are the authority.
notes.precinct_ids: A precinct's id is its county's five-digit code and its precinct code (21001A102), as the State Board writes it. listed_2026 is false for the 8 precincts of the map that the State Board's September 2026 report does not list (a military reservation, a lake, a precinct since renamed).

format.files: Every file is TopoJSON on one grid (transform above): arcs are delta-encoded lines; a shape's arcs name the lines of its rings, a negative number n meaning line ~n backwards; outer rings run counter-clockwise, holes clockwise.
format.county_files: precincts/<county>.json, object 'precincts': one shape per precinct. arcMask[i] has bit k set when line i is an outline of arc_kinds[k]; arcSides[2i] and arcSides[2i+1] are the precincts on the right and left of line i (-1: a precinct in another county's file, or one just across a hairline gap; -2: outside Kentucky); names gives the names of the places the file's precincts lie in.
format.boxes: boxes[county] holds four whole numbers a precinct, in the file's order: west, south, east, north in steps of box_step degrees from the transform's translate, rounded outwards. A point is tried against every precinct whose box (widened by half a step) holds it.

precinct_properties.name: the precinct's name (Clark Hill (D102)): its name and code in the State Board's layer
precinct_properties.precinct: the precinct's code (a letter and three digits)
precinct_properties.mcd: the city the precinct lies wholly in, or in Jefferson County the metro government (absent where it lies partly outside every city)
precinct_properties.mcd_all: list: every city the precinct reaches (in Jefferson County the metro government first), largest share first
precinct_properties.mcd_pct: list, with mcd_all: each place's share of the precinct's area, in percent
precinct_properties.ward: list: the council district the precinct lies in (Louisville Metro Council or Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council)
precinct_properties.com: magisterial district (the justice of the peace district; magistrates and constables are elected by it; absent where the letter's district is not known)
precinct_properties.circuit: judicial circuit (circuit judges and Commonwealth's attorneys; KY-JC1 to KY-JC57)
precinct_properties.sc: supreme court district (also the Court of Appeals district: 1 to 7, KRS 21A.010 and 22A.020)
precinct_properties.swcd: soil and water conservation district (the county's)
precinct_properties.listed_2026: whether the State Board's newest registration report by precinct lists the precinct
precinct_properties.school: list: the school districts the precinct lies in, largest share first
precinct_properties.school_pct: list, when the precinct is in more than one: each district's share of its area, in percent
precinct_properties.school_out: percent of the precinct's area that lies in no school district (given from 3 percent up)
precinct_properties.school_edge: list: neighbouring districts that only brush the precinct along a line (try them too when placing a point)
precinct_properties.c: a point inside the precinct's largest piece, for a label: [longitude, latitude]

ids.every layer: a shape's properties j and d are the jurisdiction id and the district its races carry on the ballot pages
ids.mcd: KY-M- and the Census Bureau's place code (KY-M-00298); KY-M-48003 the metro government; properties.t says what it is
ids.ward: <city>|<district as the council race words it> (KY-M-48003|1, KY-M-46027|12)
ids.com: <county>|<district>, magistrates and constables (21001|4, magistrates and constables)
ids.cd: the district (1); properties.race is the race for Congress
ids.swcd: KY-X-SWCD- and the county's code; j is the county
ids.school: KY-S- and the Bureau's five-digit district code (KY-S-00030)
